63678-travels-through-north-and-south-ca.creator: William Bartram.
63678-travels-through-north-and-south-ca.description: A book by William Bartram.. th-West from the sea coast—describes the face of the country, the river Savanna, the cataracts and village of Augusta—congress with the Indians at St. Augusta—the village of Wrightsborough on Little River—monuments of an ancient Indian town on Little River—Buffaloe Lick—begins the survey of the New Purchase—high proof of Indian sagacity—returns to Savanna.

64817-lunar-station.title: Lunar Station
64817-lunar-station.creator: Unknown
64817-lunar-station.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Stunned, breathless, they ducked as the _Atomic I_ blazed away from the base of Tycho's rim, her twin jets spouting trails of blazing magnificence in a double arcing trail earthward. A dazzling sight under ordinary circumstances, inconsequential now.

arxiv-1908-00262.title: Pseudo-Labeling Curriculum for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
arxiv-1908-00262.creator: Jaehoon Choi, Minki Jeong, Taekyung Kim, Changick Kim
arxiv-1908-00262.description: Abstract To learn target discriminative representations, using pseudo-labels is a simple yet effective approach for unsupervised domain adaptation. However, the existence of false pseudo-labels, which may have a detrimental influence on learning target representations, remains a major challenge. To overcome this issue, we propose a pseudo-labeling curriculum based on a density-based clustering algorithm.

arxiv-2108-04623.title: Maximizing Influence with Graph Neural Networks Thanks: Supported in part by ANR (French National Research Agency) under the JCJC project GraphIA (ANR-20-CE23-0009-01).
arxiv-2108-04623.creator: George Panagopoulos 1 , Nikolaos Tziortziotis 2 , Michalis Vazirgiannis 1 , Fragkiskos D. Malliaros 3
arxiv-2108-04623.description: Abstract Finding the seed set that maximizes the influence spread over a network is a well-known NP-hard problem. Though a greedy algorithm can provide near-optimal solutions, the subproblem of influence estimation renders the solutions inefficient. In this work, we propose Glie , a graph neural network that learns how to estimate the influence spread of the independent cascade.

arxiv-2210-05541.title: Radiation Reaction and Gravitational Waves at Fourth Post-Minkowskian Order
arxiv-2210-05541.creator: Christoph Dlapa, Gregor Kälin, Zhengwen Liu, Jakob Neef, Rafael A. Porto
arxiv-2210-05541.description: Abstract We obtain the total impulse in the scattering of non-spinning binaries in general relativity at fourth Post-Minkowskian order, i.e. 𝒪 ⁡ ( G 4 ) {\cal O}(G^{4}) , including linear, nonlinear, and hereditary radiation-reaction effects. We derive the total radiated spacetime momentum as well as the associated energy flux.

arxiv-2310-09773.title: RSVP: Customer Intent Detection via Agent Response Contrastive and Generative Pre-Training
arxiv-2310-09773.creator: Yu-Chien Tang, Wei-Yao Wang, An-Zi Yen, Wen-Chih Peng
arxiv-2310-09773.description: Abstract The dialogue systems in customer services have been developed with neural models to provide users with precise answers and round-the-clock support in task-oriented conversations by detecting customer intents based on their utterances. Existing intent detection approaches have highly relied on adaptively pre-training language models with large-scale datasets, yet the predominant cost of data collection may hinder their superiority.

arxiv-2404-14735.title: Rank2Reward: Learning Shaped Reward Functions from Passive Video
arxiv-2404-14735.creator: Daniel Yang, Davin Tjia, Jacob Berg, Dima Damen, Pulkit Agrawal, Abhishek Gupta
arxiv-2404-14735.description: Abstract Teaching robots novel skills with demonstrations via human-in-the-loop data collection techniques like kinesthetic teaching or teleoperation puts a heavy burden on human supervisors. In contrast to this paradigm, it is often significantly easier to provide raw, action-free visual data of tasks being performed. Moreover, this data can even be mined from video datasets or the web.

arxiv-2407-19946.title: Engineering an Efficient Approximate DNF-Counter
arxiv-2407-19946.creator: Mate Soos, Uddalok Sarkar, Divesh Aggarwal, Sourav Chakraborty, Kuldeep S. Meel, Maciej Obremski
arxiv-2407-19946.description: Abstract . Model counting is a fundamental problem in many practical applications, including query evaluation in probabilistic databases and failure-probability estimation of networks. In this work, we focus on a variant of this problem where the underlying formula is expressed in the Disjunctive Normal Form (DNF), also known as #DNF.

arxiv-2412-08807.title: Author:
arxiv-2412-08807.creator: Tomáš Beránek
arxiv-2412-08807.description: Abstract OPTIMALITY OF EMBEDDINGS IN ORLICZ SPACES Introduction When tasked with creating a mathematical model of a given scenario, one approach is to interpret the input data and output solutions as measurable functions, which belong to some function spaces, and the assignment of data to a solution as an operator between these spaces.

arxiv-2506-09338.title: Know What You Don’t Know: Uncertainty Calibration of Process Reward Models
arxiv-2506-09338.creator: Young-Jin Park, Kristjan Greenewald, Kaveh Alim, Hao Wang, Navid Azizan
arxiv-2506-09338.description: Abstract Process reward models (PRMs) play a central role in guiding inference-time scaling algorithms for large language models (LLMs). However, we observe that even state-of-the-art PRMs can be poorly calibrated and often overestimate success probabilities. To address this, we present a calibration approach—performed via quantile regression—that adjusts PRM outputs to better align with true success probabilities.

arxiv-2509-20804.title: Performance Consistency of Learning Methods for Information Retrieval Tasks
arxiv-2509-20804.creator: Meng Yuan, Justin Zobel
arxiv-2509-20804.description: Abstract A range of approaches have been proposed for estimating the accuracy or robustness of the measured performance of IR methods. One is to use bootstrapping of test sets, which, as we confirm, provides an estimate of variation in performance.

One clue for this disheartening outcome arises from the prognosis that asystole invariably takes place, after a time lag, on diagnosis of brain stem death. Th

Hence, the molecular characterization of pathways regulating chemosensitivity is a central prerequisite to improve cancer therapy. The hypoxia-inducible factor HIF-1α has been linke

pmc-10808806.title: Who cares about the carers? A call to action on behalf of mothers of disabled children
pmc-10808806.creator: Alison Pearson
pmc-10808806.description: This ‘perspective’ article is an urgent call to action on behalf of mothers (and indeed fathers) of disabled children in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. In doing so draws attention to the ‘perfect storm’ experienced by United Kingdom-based parents of reduced support and increased stress, coupled with the effects of isolation.

pmc-11438721.title: A Novel Stem Cell Model to Study Preeclampsia Endothelial Dysfunction
pmc-11438721.creator: Yanming Wu, Tianyanxin Sun, Pedro Medina, Purnima Narasimhan, David K. Stevenson, Frauke Von Versen-Höynck, Jennifer Armstrong, Joseph C. Wu, Nazish Sayed, Virginia D. Winn
pmc-11438721.description: Preeclampsia is a common pregnancy complication affecting 5% to 7% of all pregnancies worldwide annually. While the pathogenesis is not fully understood, maternal endothelium dysfunction is thought to be a central component to preeclampsia development. Studies to dissect maternal endothelial dysfunction, particularly on a patient-specific basis, are hampered by limited access to systemic primary endothelial cells (ECs).

pmc-11650080.title: An Image-Recognition Dietary Assessment App for Adolescents With Obesity: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-11650080.creator: Krista Oei, Elizabeth EY Choi, Alisa Bar-Dayan, Jennifer N Stinson, Mark R Palmert, Jeffrey E Alfonsi, Jill Hamilton, Amaryllis Mavragani, Bianca C Braga, Robert Marshall, Ying Chieh Liu
pmc-11650080.description: BackgroundAdolescence is a period of increased susceptibility to developing obesity-related health issues due to poor eating patterns and increased sedentary behaviors. Recommendations for pediatric obesity management include dietary assessments. However, adolescents often avoid food logging through traditional methods. The use of image-recognition dietary assessment apps in adolescents with obesity is not well studied.

pmc-12463601.title: Diagnosis and management of a rare bilateral ovarian mixed germ cell tumor: a case report
pmc-12463601.creator: Xuanling Li, Min You, Xiaoyun Zhang, Jingjing Wei, Guangyao Lin, Qianjue Tang, Lianwei Xu
pmc-12463601.description: BackgroundMixed ovarian malignant germ cell tumors (MOGCTs) are rare neoplasms composed of two or more malignant germ cell components, representing less than 1% of all ovarian germ cell tumors. They primarily affect adolescents and young women, presenting a clinical challenge due to their histologic heterogeneity, potential for recurrence, and the need to balance oncologic safety with fertility preservation.

pmc-12538057.title: Association of standard dietary inflammatory index with diabetic retinopathy in diabetes: A prospective cohort study
pmc-12538057.creator: Zihan Xu, Feipeng Jiang, Yun Zhang, Jier Ma, Jianjun Ren, Meixia Zhang
pmc-12538057.description: Background and aimsDiabetic retinopathy (DR) is a major cause of vision impairment, and its development is linked to chronic inflammation. Investigating the role of dietary patterns, specifically the standard dietary inflammatory index (DII), may provide insights into modifiable risk factors for DR.

pmc-12834227.title: Integrated omics reveals disease-associated radial glia-like cells with epigenetically dysregulated interferon response in multiple sclerosis
pmc-12834227.creator: Bongsoo Park, Alexandra M. Nicaise, Dimitrios Tsitsipatis, Liviu Pirvan, Daniel Zucha, Andi Munteanu, Pranathi Prasad, Miguel Larraz Lopez De Novales, Cristian Bulgaru, Rafael Kollyfas, Julia Whitten, Cory M. Willis, Luka Culig, Joseph Llewellyn, Rosana-Bristena Ionescu, Magdy Mekdad, Madalena B.C.
pmc-12834227.description: SUMMARYProgressive multiple sclerosis (PMS) involves a persistent, maladaptive inflammatory process with numerous cellular drivers. We generated induced neural stem cells (iNSCs) from patient fibroblasts through a direct reprogramming protocol that preserved their epigenome, which revealed a PMS-specific hypomethylation of lipid metabolism and interferon (IFN) signaling genes.

pmc-13446528.title: Performance of a Flexible Versus Rigid Fetoscope in the Simulated Management of Twin‐to‐Twin Transfusion Syndrome
pmc-13446528.creator: Emmanuel Rault, Jerome Massardier, Elsa Limouzin, Mona Massoud, Cyril Huissoud, Anthony Atallah
pmc-13446528.description: ObjectiveTo assess the feasibility and operative performance of a flexible fetoscope (FF) compared with a rigid fetoscope (RF) in the simulated management of twin‐to‐twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS) with anterior placentation.MethodA randomized, non‐blinded crossover trial was conducted during a national training session for fetal surgeons.
